speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your symptoms. Are you experiencing any difficulty speaking or swallowing along with your double vision, limb weakness, and trouble climbing stairs? Also, have you noticed any recent changes in your balance or coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very specific. Given your symptoms of double vision, limb weakness, and difficulty climbing stairs, I need to check your muscle strength and reflexes immediately. REQUEST TEST: Full_Neurological_Examination.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Cranial_Nerves: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze; Motor_Strength: Diminished motor strength observed in the upper extremities, with normal tone and no obvious atrophy; Reflexes: Normal reflexes throughout; Sensation: Normal sensation throughout.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ptosis worsening with sustained gaze, diplopia, and fluctuating muscle weakness that improves with rest is classic for this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend ordering a Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone (TSH) test to rule out Lambert-Eaton syndrome and a Chest_CT to check for an associated thymoma. REQUEST TEST: TSH. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT.
